abstract: **s******u**sticle mortality in** **nuit communities in** **canada : rates and effects of community characteristics.** in absence of **i**nuit specific data in vital statistics in canada, one can rely on a geographical approach to produce a demographic analysis of mortality in **i**nuit communities in canada. in this way we have estimated suicide mortality in the four regions of canada where **i**nuit communities are located : nunavut, nunavik (north of quebec), nunatsiavut (labrador) and the **i**nuivaluit region (north west territories) for the periods 19891993, 19941998 and 19992003. the analysis reveals suicide rates 6 to 11 times higher in the **i**nuit regions as a whole, wide variations in rates between one **i**nuit region and another, and a sharp rise in rates during the most recent period analysed. the estimated suicide rates have been matched with the 2001 canadian census and the 2001 aboriginal peoples survey produced by statistics canada, in order to identify some explanatory factors.
